paper_metadata.title: Python-Integrated Quantum–Classical Computing Framework for Intelligent Time-Series Prediction

summary: The paper presents a Python-integrated hybrid variational quantum-classical time-series predictor using Qiskit Aer simulation on financial and synthetic datasets. It reports 93.7% accuracy versus 89.3% for classical baselines, MSE of 0.014, correlation of 0.92, 22% lower training time, and 18% lower execution latency, but only in simulation and without a demonstrated practical quantum advantage.

experiments.description: Python-integrated hybrid quantum-classical time-series prediction using variational quantum circuits with Qiskit Aer simulation on synthetic and real financial datasets, compared against classical baselines.

algorithm.variant: variational quantum circuit (VQC) time-series predictor with classical optimizer
algorithm.ansatz: parameterized rotation gates with entanglement layers
algorithm.optimizer: Adam or SGD (paper mentions both; exact optimizer per run not specified)
algorithm.convergence_criteria: training stops at convergence or after all encoded instances are processed; loss curves generally converge after about 35 iterations

problem_formulation.encoding_details: raw time-series windows are normalized, windowed, and mapped to quantum states via rotation gate parameters; expectation values are used as classical feature vectors
problem_formulation.objective_function: minimize combined loss L_total = alpha * L_quantum + (1 - alpha) * L_classical

problem_instance.description: Time-series forecasting for financial and synthetic nonlinear sequences

dataset_specification.FIN-Daily: daily aggregated financial series; price, volume; approx. 30,000 records; window size 60
dataset_specification.FIN-Intra: high-frequency intraday financial series; price, bid/ask; approx. 120,000 records; window size 50
dataset_specification.SYN-Nonlin: synthetic nonlinear control data; engineered trends/noise; approx. 50,000 records; window size 60
dataset_specification.preprocessing: missing values removed; normalization; time-ordered split; z-score scaling; fixed-length windowing; angle encoding

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: cleaning, normalization, z-score scaling, time-ordered split to avoid look-ahead, fixed-length windowing, angle encoding, early stopping, grid/random search for hyperparameters
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: multiple repeated runs with fixed seeds and error bars; ablation studies; scalability tests across varying qubit counts and circuit depths; comparison against LSTM, GRU, and shallow feedforward baseline

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Pandas/NumPy preprocessing, normalization, windowing, z-score scaling, train/val/test split
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: expectation values assembled into Python dict; predictions saved with checkpoints

speedup_claims.conditions: reported for the hybrid model on the paper's experiments
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports percentage reduction in training time, not absolute wall-clock time; exact baseline timing is not given.
